title: Fable 5 benchmark results compared with other models
author: lagerskoy
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
CLAUDE FABLE 5 IS PLAYING A DIFFERENT GAME

Same prompts, same tasks, same rules, yet the outputs don't even feel like they came from the same generation of AI. While other models produced decent simulations, Claude Fable 5 generated scenes that look closer to finished products than experiments. The fluid simulation has more depth, the lunar environment feels like an actual game world, and the black hole render looks like something pulled from a modern visualization engine rather than a chatbot response.

What's interesting isn't that one model won a benchmark. It's that the gap is becoming visible without charts, scores, or leaderboards. You can see it instantly. When people can identify the stronger model from a few seconds of video, the conversation shifts from "which AI is best" to "how far ahead is it"

The most dangerous thing about AI progress is that it happens gradually, then all at once. This video feels a lot like one of those moments.
summary: Shares updated coding-agent benchmark results and positions Claude Fable 5 against other frontier coding agents.

Someone prompted Claude Fable 5 to generate the entire journey of a baby developing in the womb. It built a fully explorable, first-person 3D world. In a browser. From a single prompt.

Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's first publicly available Mythos-class model, released June 9, 2026. You describe a world in plain language. It builds the whole thing, with full 3D rendering, playable directly in your browser.

This is the same model that rendered Borges's "Library of Babel" as a 3D game where you pull books off infinite shelves and climb spiral staircases. The same model that built a to-scale Yosemite Valley with 266,000 individually placed trees using real NASA elevation data, all in a single session.

On Anthropic's senior engineer benchmark, Fable 5 scored 91/100. The previous flagship scored 63.

Now someone walked through the womb.

We are not building apps anymore. We are building worlds.

#AI #ClaudeFable5 #Anthropic

originalText:
Claude Fable 5 shipped today. The model isn't the lecture. The metric is.

Anthropic tracks one number for Claude: time horizon how long an agent stays coherent on a single goal before drifting.

Claude Opus 4 could build a feature. Six months ago: an overnight run. 

Fable 5: days on one goal, per the keynote.

The practical part nobody writes down:

Keep your dead prototypes. The ones that almost worked. Re-run them on every Claude release. 

They're your private eval for the exponential.

Most teams test the new Claude on tasks that already worked. That measures nothing.

When a broken prototype flips to working that's the signal. Ship that week.

The capability didn't arrive. It was scheduled. Your prototypes are the calendar.

originalText:
FABLE 5 ONE-SHOT A CALL OF DUTY ZOMBIES CLONE FROM A SINGLE LAZY PROMPT

No planning mode.

No back-and-forth.

No hours of prompting Claude.

Just one sentence:

"Make me a COD Zombies clone, single-player, and make the shooting feel good."

And Fable 5 shipped a playable game.

What came back:

a fully playable FPS in the browser
surprisingly satisfying movement and gunplay
most features worked on the first try
built entirely with Three.js
no game engine
no assets
no elaborate spec document

A few months ago, building something like this meant days of work.

Now it's a one-line prompt.

The distance between "I have an idea" and "I'm playing it" is collapsing fast.

We're entering an era where vibe-coding an entire game is becoming a one-sentence problem.
